### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/service-record-context`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **32** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0088bbb8fec784e3a8e6d6b9e564ccb3e14f6eb`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/lint/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/ai.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/ai.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0088bbb8fec784e3a8e6d6b9e564ccb3e14f6eb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b1ce322417d949f19f2b9da92a85cbc268e02a0e` — the merge of head `bb0107ccadaab70025c410545408414395527a26` into base `d0088bbb8fec784e3a8e6d6b9e564ccb3e14f6eb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b1ce322417d949f19f2b9da92a85cbc268e02a0e && git checkout b1ce322417d949f19f2b9da92a85cbc268e02a0e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d0088bbb8fec784e3a8e6d6b9e564ccb3e14f6eb bb0107ccadaab70025c410545408414395527a26 && git checkout -B drift-repro d0088bbb8fec784e3a8e6d6b9e564ccb3e14f6eb && git merge --no-ff bb0107ccadaab70025c410545408414395527a26

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d0088bbb8fec784e3a8e6d6b9e564ccb3e14f6eb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d0088bbb8fec784e3a8e6d6b9e564ccb3e14f6eb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `aa76b901be459a8271b412ad9fcb099024a7fb33`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/ai-context.zod.ts + packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/door.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts

Inputs read: card #37203 (body and all 8 comments), PR #37354 body and file list (21 files), the net diff against `main`, the check-runs on this head (no failure; every required run success or skipped). Read to judge, not reviewed: `docs/adr/0160-record-scoped-ai-inquiry.md` (D1, D3, D4, points 13 to 21, row 11), `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/query.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/context-tokens.zod.ts`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts`, `packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts#recordContextMembers`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `related[]` accept set widened by three optional keys (`where`, `orderBy`, `limit`); a pack without them parses and reads exactly as before. Right: ADR-0160 row 11, `Metadata-protocol: added`.
- `where` is `FilterConditionSchema` plus one refinement walk, so it is a strict subset of the object filter form and the base form's comparand refusals still run. Read against ADR D1: the ten operators and `$and` / `$or` admitted; `$not`, every other `$` key, a dotted key, a nested condition on a lookup's target, `{ $field }`, `$now`, an object comparand, a whole `{token}` string (also as an `$in` / `$nin` member), a nested list and an empty operator map are each refused; a bare value is `$eq`; a string that only contains braces stays a literal. Right.
- `orderBy` is `SortNodeSchema[]` with `.min(1)` and an own-field name check. `orderBy: []` is refused, which the ADR's words do not state; an empty order means nothing, so right.
- `limit` is an integer from 1 to `AI_CONTEXT_MAX_RELATED_ROWS` (20), and `RECORD_CONTEXT_RELATED_MAX_ROWS` now reads that constant. Right: point 14, one number. The service constant's type widens from the literal `20` to `number`; additive.
- The aliases `filter`, `sort`, `sortBy` change a refusal's message only (the object was already strict). The schema-level `guidance.filter` text now points at the entry's `where`. Right.
- New public exports of `@objectstack/spec/ai`: `AI_CONTEXT_MAX_RELATED_ROWS`, `AI_CONTEXT_WHERE_OPERATORS`, `AI_CONTEXT_WHERE_COMBINATORS`, `aiContextWhereFields`, `AiContextRelatedWhereSchema` and its two types. Additive; api-surface and export-origins moved with them and their gates are green.
- `RecordContextDoor.query` takes an optional `orderBy`, and the door gains the optional `queryableFieldsOf`. Additive for a door implementer. Both in-tree doors pass `query` options through unchanged (read in `recordContextMembers` and the stdio bridge's `query`), so `orderBy` reaches the engine.
- Lint: `ai-context-field-unknown` now also fires for a `where` / `orderBy` field the child lacks. No existing pack can carry those keys, so no existing pack gains a warning. Right.
- The published JSON Schema for `where` and `orderBy` is wider than the Zod type; the new sites are in `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` and the gate is green. Right: new rules entering the ledger, no existing exemption widened.
- The read set is unchanged: `planObjectsOf` takes nothing from the three keys (D4). Right.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-record-context` and `@objectstack/lint`. The diff adds authorable keys (`Metadata-protocol: added`, which takes at least `minor` on each package it moves) and removes or narrows nothing an author could write before. `Check Changeset` is success.
Clause-②: yes. The line stands in the PR body and in the changeset body, with no arm, and matches the diff.

### ③ Boundary flags

- SQL push-down: holds. `where`, `orderBy` and `limit` all go into the one child query (`$and` with the link filter, `limit + 1` probe). No new id materialisation and no in-app join, filter or sort. The added probes (`queryableFieldsOf`, `fieldVisibilityOf`) are metadata reads, at most one per related entry.
- `open_questions`: none in the report.
- Dev flag, parity acceptance PARTIAL: the card's line "same answer on MCP stdio and HTTP" has no `where`-pack case, because `packages/mcp` and `packages/runtime` were fenced. Accepted as carried, not as met. Escalated to the seat: the parity case needs a card before this PR closes #37203.
- Dev flag, neither real door supplies `queryableFieldsOf`: on real doors the fallback decides (served, not withheld, no `maskingRule`). That is the fallback the `getQueryableFields` contract and ADR D3 name, and it covers the card's "ordinary caller". A field the security answer excludes but the fallback admits (an agent acting for a person, a computed field reading a hidden one) still reaches the engine guard, which refuses the whole call: fail-closed, and against D3's "that refusal is never reached". Escalated to the seat: the door card (`packages/runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts#recordContextMembers`, `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts`) has no carrier yet and needs one.
- Dev flag, triage row 7154563681 (a related child this caller is not served is left out) implemented and reverted: answered, the tree at this head still refuses and the PR body says so. Escalated to the seat: the PR body says `Fixes #37203`, and the card's row is unchecked, so the row needs its own card before the merge closes this one.
- Dev flag, Studio does not offer the three keys: answered, carried by #37143 (note 7168171718).
- Dev flag, `RecordContextNoteKind` prose says a cut "at the row cap": see N1.
- Dev flag, a door page cap below `limit + 1`: see N2.
- Dev flag, the baseline ledger grew: answered in ①.
- Dev flag, stale PR body: answered, the body at this head names `aa76b901b`, 96 tests and the revert.
- Dev flag, commit trailers: not a contract matter; the lane seat's.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/ai/ai-context.zod.ts`, against ADR-0160 D1 (second amendment) and its first consumer, `executeGetRecordContext`: the schema holds, with one hole.

S1 (should-fix) — `aiContextWhereFields` stops walking at depth 32, while `checkRelatedWhere` and `FilterConditionSchema` admit any nesting. A `where` nested deeper than 32 combinators parses, and the fields it names below that depth are in no list: the service does not judge them (neither "the child lacks it" nor "the caller cannot query on it"), the lint rule does not report them, and the query still runs with them. With the security plugin the engine guard then refuses the whole call for a caller who cannot query on such a field, which D3 says never happens; an unknown field reaches the engine. The two walks of one tree must agree: refuse nesting past a bound at parse (row 11 invites one, "refused at parse like the pack's other bounds"), or drop the cap. Pin the boundary by test.

`packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts` and `door.ts`, sentence by sentence against D3: one capped query; the link filter joined with `$and` (a top-level `$or` in `where` cannot reach another root); `orderBy` passed; `limit + 1` probe and the cut stated at `plan.cap`; a field the published definition lacks leaves the section out and states nothing; a field the caller cannot query on drops the section with the one statement and is never named; a throwing probe drops the section. The door answer path requires the field to be served as well as queryable. All agree with the contract. One case is not judged:

S2 (should-fix) — an `orderBy` on a field its author declared `sortable: false` is not judged anywhere. The stdio door's `query` refuses it before the engine (`unofferedSortRefusal`, `INVALID_SORT`, "Query parameter 'orderBy' sorts by ..."), and the executor does not catch it, so such a pack validates clean and then fails every call for every caller, with an error that blames a parameter the caller never sent. It is an author defect, and ADR D1 puts author defects on author surfaces while the answer states nothing. Report it in `validate-ai-context.ts` (and leave the section out in the executor, as for a field the child lacks), or have the seat rule it out of this card with a follow-up. Read on the stdio door only; the HTTP door's verdict was not read, so the parity line may also be at stake.

`packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts`: extends the #37176 rule, reads the same `aiContextWhereFields` as the service, reports at `related[i].where` and `related[i].orderBy[k].field`, and its message matches what the service does (the list is left out). Agrees with D1, subject to S1 and S2.

Nits, none affecting correctness on the in-tree doors:
- N1 (nit) — `RecordContextNoteKind`'s doc line (`packages/spec/src/ai/record-context-tools.zod.ts`, outside the diff) still says `related_truncated` is a cut "at the row cap"; it now also fires at `limit`. Follow-up card.
- N2 (nit) — ADR D1 and point 14 say a door whose own page cap is below a parsed `limit` cuts there "and the cut is stated". The executor cannot see such a cut (it compares against `plan.cap`), and `door.ts` does not say what a door owes. The stdio door passes `limit` through, so nothing in the tree reaches it as read; the HTTP bridge's cap was not read. Follow-up card.
- N3 (nit) — `AiContextRelatedWhere` is typed as the whole `FilterCondition`, wider than the admitted subset, so the type admits `$not` and the others that parse refuses. Accepted deviation.
- N4 (nit) — the `limit` describe reads "(at most 20, the default)"; the default is the row cap, which is the same number, but the sentence reads as if 20 were `limit`'s default value. Accepted deviation.
- N5 (nit) — no test pins an `orderBy` on a registry-injected field (`created_at`), the likely order for "the latest rows". Whether the lint field map and the published definition both carry it was not established by reading. Follow-up card.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37203-related-where-orderby-limit`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bb0107ccadaab70025c410545408414395527a26`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/ai/ai-context.zod.ts + packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts, packages/services/service-record-context/src/door.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts, packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts, packages/lint/src/index.ts

Delta review of the round on `aa76b901be459a8271b412ad9fcb099024a7fb33`. Inputs read: card #37203 with its comments, the delta report among them (7179036175); the PR body at this head; the delta `aa76b901b..bb0107cca` (13 files); the check-runs on this head (no failure; every required run success or skipped). Read to judge, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/api/sortability.zod.ts#resolveObjectSortability`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-query-validation.ts` (`assertSortFieldsExist`, `assertSortFieldsAreOffered`, `UNMATERIALIZED_SORT_TYPES`), `packages/mcp/src/stdio-data-bridge.ts#unofferedSortRefusal`, `packages/spec/src/data/search-fields.ts#SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`. The sections below judge the whole PR at this head; what the earlier round settled and the delta did not touch is carried.

### ① Derived judgments

- Carried from the earlier round, unchanged by the delta: `related[]` widened by the optional `where`, `orderBy` and `limit`; `where` a strict subset of the object filter form; `limit` bounded by the one number `AI_CONTEXT_MAX_RELATED_ROWS`; the aliases and `guidance.filter` text; the additive door members; the unchanged read set. All right.
- New in the delta: `where` refuses `$and` / `$or` nested more than `AI_CONTEXT_WHERE_MAX_DEPTH` (32) lists deep. It narrows only what the earlier head of this same PR admitted, which was never published. Right: ADR-0160 row 11 invites the bound, "refused at parse like the pack's other bounds".
- New public export `AI_CONTEXT_WHERE_MAX_DEPTH` in `@objectstack/spec/ai`; api-surface and export-origins moved with it. Additive.
- New lint rule id `ai-context-sort-field-unsortable` (a warning) and its exported constant `AI_CONTEXT_SORT_FIELD_UNSORTABLE`. It can fire only on a pack that carries `orderBy`, which no pack on `main` can. Right.
- The executor now leaves out, silently and for every caller, a related section whose `orderBy` names a field the child's sortability projection calls unsortable. Before the delta both doors refused that call whole. Right: an author defect, treated as the "field the definition lacks" arm is.
- `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/service-record-context` now import `resolveObjectSortability` from `@objectstack/spec/api`. Both already depend on the spec package; type checks are green.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/service-record-context` and `@objectstack/lint`, unchanged and still right: the delta adds one export and one rule id and removes nothing published. The changeset body now states the nesting bound and the unsortable-order rule. `Check Changeset` is success.
Clause-②: yes. The line stands in the PR body and in the changeset body, with no arm.

### ③ Boundary flags

- SQL push-down: holds. The delta adds no read: the sortability verdict is computed from the published definition the executor already holds, and an unsortable order skips the query.
- `open_questions`: none in the delta report.
- Dev flag, S2 covers a formula as well as `sortable: false`: answered and accepted, see ④.
- Dev flag, `packages/lint/src/index.ts` and `rule-explanations.ts` join the touched files: answered, they are the rule's wiring and are in Scope above.
- Dev flag, N1, N2 and N5 not taken, carried by #37361: accepted as carried.
- Dev flag, PR #37366 conflicts in the generated `packages/spec/export-origins/ai.json`: the lane seat's; whichever lands second regenerates the file.
- Dev flags on push order (a push not gated on its overlap check; a push before the whole lint package ran) and commit trailers: not contract matters; the lane seat's. CI on this head is green.
- Still escalated to the seat from the earlier round, and not answered by this delta: (1) the card's stdio/HTTP parity line has no `where`-pack case and needs a card; (2) neither real door supplies `queryableFieldsOf`, so a caller the security answer excludes but the fallback admits still gets a whole-call refusal from the engine guard, and that door card needs a carrier; (3) the PR body says `Fixes #37203` while triage row 7154563681 is unchecked and not in this PR, so the row needs its own card before the merge closes this one.

### ④ Design judgment

S1: closed
S2: closed

`packages/spec/src/ai/ai-context.zod.ts`. `checkRelatedWhere` carries a depth that counts the `$and` / `$or` lists a condition sits beneath, and refuses a list that would put a condition at depth 33. `aiContextWhereFields` walks conditions down to depth 32 by the same constant and skips only members at depth 33, which parse has already refused. Read side by side, the two walks agree at the boundary: every field of a `where` that parsed is listed. The test pins 32 accepted, with the innermost field named, and 33 refused; the report's ablation of the bound went red.

`packages/services/service-record-context/src/record-context-tools.ts`. An `orderBy` field with `sortable === false` in `resolveObjectSortability(published definition)` leaves the section out before the query, after the "definition lacks it" check and before the caller-specific check, so the answer is the same for every caller and states nothing. A `where` on such a field still reads, which is right: the doors' verdict is on the sort axis only.

The formula widening, against both doors' actual predicate. `resolveObjectSortability` answers `sortable: false` for two reasons: `virtual-type` (`isVirtualSearchField`, `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`, today `formula` alone) and `author-declared` (the literal `sortable: false`). The stdio door refuses by that same function (`unofferedSortRefusal`: `projection[f]?.sortable === false`), so it refuses both reasons. The HTTP door refuses `sortable: false` by that same function (`assertSortFieldsAreOffered`) and a formula by `UNMATERIALIZED_SORT_TYPES`, today `formula` alone. So the executor's predicate is exactly what each door refuses, and the widening holds; judging `sortable: false` alone would have left a formula order refusing the whole call on both doors. No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/lint/src/validate-ai-context.ts`, `rule-explanations.ts`, `index.ts`. The rule reads the same projection as the executor and the doors, reports at `related[i].orderBy[k].field`, reports an unknown field as `ai-context-field-unknown` first and never both, and its message matches what the executor does. Its wiring matches its sibling `ai-context-body-not-long-text` site for site: the constant in `validate-ai-context.ts`, the re-export in `index.ts`, the explanation and its `RULE_EXPLANATIONS` entry. The explanation's `covers` length pin is green on this head.

Tried and not broken: a pack with both an unknown and an unsortable order field (left out by the first check); an order on `id` (the projection answers sortable); a `where`-only entry (no sortability read); a lint run over array-shaped or map-shaped `fields` (the projection's reader takes both).

Nits, none affecting correctness on the in-tree doors:
- N1 (nit) — `RecordContextNoteKind`'s doc line (outside the diff) still says `related_truncated` is a cut "at the row cap"; it now also fires at `limit`. Carried by #37361.
- N2 (nit) — ADR-0160 point 14 says a cut at a door's lower page cap is stated; the executor cannot see such a cut and `door.ts` does not say what a door owes. Nothing in the tree reaches it as read. Carried by #37361.
- N3 (nit) — `AiContextRelatedWhere` is typed as the whole `FilterCondition`, wider than what parse admits. Accepted deviation.
- N4 (nit) — the `limit` describe reads "(at most 20, the default)", which reads as if 20 were `limit`'s default. Accepted deviation.
- N5 (nit) — no test pins an `orderBy` on a registry-injected field such as `created_at`. Carried by #37361.
- N6 (nit) — ADR-0160 D1 lists the author defects reported on author surfaces and does not name an unsortable `orderBy` field; the code now goes one step past the record's words. Follow-up card for an ADR line.
- N7 (nit) — the HTTP door's formula verdict reads `UNMATERIALIZED_SORT_TYPES` and the projection reads `SEARCH_VIRTUAL_TYPES`: two one-member sets that agree today. If one grows alone, the executor and the HTTP door part. Outside the diff; follow-up card.
- N8 (nit) — the liveness evidence for `related.orderBy.field` does not mention the sortability verdict. Accepted deviation.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-37203-related-where-orderby-limit`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Utp6CYtTDvfPQDzMbZnN5X`

**VERDICT: PASS**
